chunks: Ali ibn Muhammad, from Sahl ibn Ziyad, from Ismail ibn Mihran, who said:
I wrote to Al-Reza (peace be upon him) asking him about the extent of the face, so he wrote: 'From the beginning of the hair to the end of the face, and likewise the two foreheads.'

key_terms.آخِرِ الْوَجْهِ: The end of the face (chin/lower jaw)
key_terms.حَدِّ الْوَجْهِ: The limit or extent of the face

ai.seo_question: What is the exact boundary of the face to be washed in wudu according to Imam Al-Reza?
ai.summary: In this concise reply, Imam al-Rida (peace be upon him) clarifies the anatomical boundaries for washing the face during ablution, defining the extent from the hairline to the chin and including the two foreheads. This narration is pivotal in Shia jurisprudence for establishing the precise limits of the face, distinguishing it from the neck and arms, and ensuring the validity of wudu according to the Ahl al-Bayt's interpretation of ritual purity.

en.hubeali: Ali Bin Muhammad, from Sahl Bin Ziyad, from Ismail Bin Mihran who said,

‘I wrote to Al-Rezaasws asking himasws about the extent of the face (to be washed for the Ablution (Wudhu)). So heasws wrote: ‘From the beginning of the hair up to the end of the face, and like that are the two brows’.
en.sarwar: 4. Ali ibn Muhammad has narrated from Sahl ibn Ziyad from ’Isma‘il ibn Mehran who has said the following: “
I wrote to al-Rida, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, and asked him about the limits of the area of the face. He wrote this back to me, ‘It is from the hairline down to the end and (beginning of) both brows.’”
